Yes, but only with `--dry-run`:

```bash
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

A team memory notes that **in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket.** A real run against staging would write to prod.

Details:
- The script takes its bucket from the `EXPORT_BUCKET` environment variable (`scripts/export.py:10`). It only falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev` when that variable isn't set. Whatever staging sets is what the script uses.
- Right now the script just prints `exporting staging to <bucket> (dry_run=...)` and doesn't upload anything (`scripts/export.py:11`). Even so, use `--dry-run` every time. Once real upload logic is added, a run without it will hit prod.
- The printed line shows which bucket was picked up, so a dry run confirms the bucket mix-up without risk.

If you want to test real writes, set `EXPORT_BUCKET` to a scratch bucket for that one command instead of using staging's value. Better still, fix staging's config so it stops pointing at prod.
